2.  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote Teleconference/Virtual City Council Meetings
  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  At the November 16, 2021 City Council meeting, the City Council made findings pursuant
  to Assembly Bill 361 to continue to meet remotely. To continue this practice, it is required,
  that the City Council determine that the COVID-1 9 state of emergency proclaimed by the
  Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
  to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or
  recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and
  that as a result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent
  risks to the health or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be made every
  thirty (30) days, the City Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming January
  17, 2023 meeting and thirty (30) days thereafter.
  Recommended Action
  Determine that the COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists
  and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue to have
  teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
  measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result
  of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the
  health or safety of attendees.

3.  Photo Booth Encroachment and Lease Agreement
  In 2017, the City Council approved an encroachment permit for Shana Cassidy, dba
  Catalina Photobooth. The permit was approved for a location near the intersection of
  Pebbly Beach Road and Crescent Avenue. The permit was approved for a three-year
  period and expired in May 2020.
  Recommended Action
  1. Approve an encroachment permit for a five year period for the continued use of a photo
  booth operated by Catalina Photobooth at the intersection of Pebbly Beach Road and
  Crescent Avenue, 2. Authorize the City Manager to approve future encroachment permits
  for Catalina Photobooth. 3. Authorize the City Manager to execute a lease agreement for
  the area with terms as outlined in the Staff Report.

4.  Authorize the City Manager to Dispense with Competitive Purchasing Process Catalina
  --

  Boatyard Inc. and Diversified Composites Inc.
  The City of Avalon’s Municipal Code (AMC) Chapter 3-4 outlines procedures for the
  procurement of services, supplies and equipment. The AMC requires competitive
  processes be used for purchases between $25,000 and $60,000. However, in specific
  circumstances, Section 3-4.111 outlines exceptions from bidding and other competitive
  procedures.
  Recommended Action
  Determine a competitive market does not exist for the maintenance of City-owned floats
  and authorize the City Manager or his designee to dispense with the competitive
  purchasing process and designate Catalina Boatyard Inc. and Diversified Composites
  Inc. vendors meeting the Economic Efficiency standard as outlined in the Avalon
  Municipal Code section 3-4.111 (c).

5.  Consideration of a Planning Commission Resolution Recommending City Council
  Adoption of the Annual Growth Policy for 2023
  The Avalon Municipal Code stipulates that the City Council, in conjunction with the
  Planning Commission, shall review the growth permitted in the preceding ten months,
  review the effects and demands of such development and any additional development
  upon the City’s natural resources, and determine, by resolution, the amount and type of
  growth the City will permit in the succeeding year, as well as City priorities for growth.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution establishing the City of Avalon’s Annual Growth Policy for 2023.

GENERAL BUSINESS

6.  Cruise Ship Annual Report for the year ending December 31, 2022
  In 2020, the City Council adopted a resolution establishing guidelines for the approval of
  cruise ships visiting Avalon through 2022. The resolution further requires Staff to provide
  an annual report on cruise ship vessels that includes the number of vessels, number of
  passengers, amount of wharfage collected, any safety or security incidents, as well as
  projections and scheduling information for the next year.
  Recommended Action
  Receive and file the Cruise Ship Annual Report for the calendar year ending December
  20, 2022 and adopt a resolution establishing the approval guidelines for cruise ships.

SUBJECT:  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote TeleconferenceNirtual City
  Council Meetings Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Determine that the COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed
by the Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result of the
COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety
of attendees.

REPORT SUMMARY: Traditionally, the Brown Act allows for teleconference or virtual meetings,
provided that the physical locations of the legislative body’s members joining by teleconference
are posted on the agenda, that those locations are open to the public and that a quorum of the
members is located within its jurisdiction. Newly enacted AB 361 provides an exception to these
procedures in order to allow for fully virtual meetings during proclaimed emergencies, including
the COVID-19 pandemic.

Since March of 2020 and the issuance of Governor Newsom’s Executive Order N-29-20, which
suspended portions of the Brown Act relating to teleconferencing, the City Council has had virtual
meetings without having to post the location of the legislative body members attending virtually.
Most public agencies have been holding public meetings using virtual platforms since this time.
In June of 2021, Governor Newsom issued Executive Order N-08-21, which provided that the
exceptions contained in EO N-29-20 would sunset on September 30: 2021.

On September 10, 2021, the Legislature adopted AB 361, which allows public agencies to hold
fully virtual meetings under certain circumstances without the posting of the agenda from each
location a legislative body member is attending. Governor Newsom signed the bill into law on
September 16, 2021. Because it contained an urgency provision, it took immediate effect.

Specific Findings Required underAB 361

Under AB 361, the City Council can hold virtual meetings without providing notice of the City
Council’s teleconference location if the City Council makes the determination that there is a
Governor-proclaimed state of emergency, which the City Council will consider in their
determination, and one of two secondary criteria listed below exists:

  1. State or local officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social
  distancing in connection with COVID-19; or

6509.00034520811
   2. The City Council determines that requiring a meeting in person would present an
  imminent risk to the health or safety of attendees.

COVID-19 continues to present an imminent threat to the health or safety of members of the
public, and the Governor’s declaration of a COVID-19 emergency still exists. Although vaccines
are now widely available, many people in the State and County are still not fully vaccinated and
remain susceptible to infection. The disease can still spread rapidly through person-to-person
contact and those in close proximity. Further, more contagious variants of the disease are now
present in the State and County, the most predominant of which is a new variant of the Omnicron
variant. The County of Los Angeles recently re-instituted some mandates given the rise in cases
and deaths nationally and public health officials have indicated that they may reinstitute certain
mask requirements if cases continue to rise. The City’s economy is dependent upon visitors to
the island, the presence of which, increases the likelihood of transmission of the disease. Also,
having members of the public attend council meetings at locations where council members are
in attendance due to their desire to avoid exposure to COVID-19 poses an imminent risk to the
health or safety of attendees.

Re-Authorization is Required Within 30 Days

SUBJECT:  Authorize the City Manager to Dispense with Competitive
  Purchasing Process Catalina Boatyard Inc. and Diversified
  --

  Composites Inc.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Determine a competitive market does not exist for the
maintenance of City-owned floats and authorize the City Manager or his designee to dispense
with the competitive purchasing process and designate Catalina Boatyard Inc. and Diversified
Composites Inc. vendors meeting the Economic Efficiency standard as outlined in the Avalon
Municipal Code section 3-4.111(c).

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon’s Municipal Code (AMC) Chapter 3-4 outlines
procedures for the procurement of services, supplies and equipment, to ensure procurement at
the lowest possible cost commensurate with quality. The process also allows the City and City
Council to exercise positive financial control over purchases, clearly define the authority for the
purchases function, and to assure the quality of purchases.
The AMC requires competitive processes be used including formal bidding, informal bidding,
vendor price quotes or REPs. However, in specific circumstances, Section 3-4.111 outlines
exceptions from bidding and other competitive procedures, including:

  •  Emergencies.
  •  Sole Source Vendors.
  •  Economic Efficiency.
  •  Cooperative Purchases.
  •  Or as authorized by state or federal law.

Since the procurement policy was adopted in 2018, City Staff have attempted to procure the
necessary documentation through formal bidding, informal bidding, vendor quotes, proposals,
etc. as required to demonstrate a competitive process has been implemented for the
construction and maintenance of City owned and maintained floats. This includes floats
constructed of a wooden and fiberglass structure or a steel structure. It has been found to be a
regionally specialized procurement for the respective materials with very limited vendors. Due
to geographical restrictions (work needs to be completed in a dry dock either on island or in
close proximity on the mainland) and the nature of the specialized scope of work necessary, it
has been determined that a competitive market does not exist for the construction and
maintenance of these floats, For steel floats only one vendor, Al Larsen’s Boatyard in San Pedro
has been responsive to the City’s past efforts to procure services. In response, the City Council
determined that this vendor was a sole source vendor for these services. Similarly for wood and
 fiberglass floats only two vendors within our region have been responsive for these
procurements including Catalina Boatyard Inc. in Avalon and Diversified Composites Inc. in San
Pedro. Another constraint in procuring work on these floats is the work window to complete a
project is highly sensitive to visitor season on the island. There is only a very limited time of year
that a float can be removed from the harbor and it doesn’t have a significant impact on
operations. So, even the competition between the two vendors is usually not efficient as it
depends on the capacity to get the work accomplished within the work flow in the respective
boat yard. It is also important to note that “Public Works” project definitions have different
procurement requirements. In this instance, these floats do not fit that description since they are
not a fixed facility and all proposed work occurs in a private boat yard, similar to work on a vessel.
According to the AMC Sec. 3-4. 111(c) Economic Efficiency. If a competitive market does not
exist, or the City will not gain a competitive advantage by using the formal contract bid or other
competitive procedure, or where the public project, goods or services may be obtained more
economically or efficiently without the procedure, the City may dispense with formal bidding or
other competitive procedures.
City Staff recommend the City Council determines a competitive market does not exist and
authorizes the City Manager or his designee to dispense with the competitive purchasing
process and designate Catalina Boatyard Inc. and Diversified Composites Inc. vendors meeting
the Economic Efficiency standard as outlined in the AMC Section 3-4.111(c).
If authorized, rather than implementing the time consuming process of attempting to solicit bids
or proposals, City Staff may immediately contract with Catalina Boatyard Inc. or Diversified
Composites Inc. to begin restoration of the City’s floats. Each contract award will still be brought
to City Council for approval, this approval will only define the procurement process for these
limited type of projects.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Undetermined.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Maintenance of City
owned floats will not be expedited efficiently, the process will be slowed down as Staff will be
required to attempt to demonstrate a competitive process is taking place.

approval process required by cruise ships wishing to visit Avalon; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Avalon City Council will review and reapprove the
established guidelines every two years.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
OF AVALON:

  1. Numberofregularly scheduled cruise ship vessels shall not exceed 3 per week
  during the Summer Season (Memorial Day to Labor Day) without final written
  approval of the City Manager.

  2. No cruise ship vessels shall be allowed on the weekends during the Summer
  Season (Memorial Day to Labor Day) or during special event weekends such —

  as Jazz Traxx —without final written approval of the City Manager.

  3. Number of regularly scheduled cruise ship vessels shall not exceed 3 per week
  during the ‘Off Season” (Labor Day to Memorial Day) without final written
  approval of the City Manager.

  4. Repositioning, infrequent, or small cruise ship vessels (1,000 passengers or
  less) may be considered for visitation by the Harbor Master, taking into account
  the day requested, holidays, event(s), harbor activity(ies), impacts to public
  safety, etc.

  5. The Harbor Master and Finance Director will provide an annual report on cruise
  ship vessels that includes the number of vessels that visit Avalon, number of
  passengers, amount of wharfage collected, any safety or security incidents that
  may have occurred while the ship was in port, as well as projections and
  scheduling information for the next year.
   6. Guidelines shall be reviewed and re-established by a City Council adopted
  resolution based on the findings of the annual reports.
